newsitem.title: USA: Biogen's MS drug clears European market hurdle.
newsitem.headline: Biogen's MS drug clears European market hurdle.

text.p: Biogen Inc cleared another hurdle toward introducing its rapidly growing drug to treat relapsing multiple sclerosis to the European market when a key agency issued a positive opinion of the drug.

The interferon beta-1a drug, which will be marketed under the brand name Avonex, received a positive opinion from the Committee for Proprietary Medicinal Products, the Cambridge, Mass.-based biotechnology company said.
Biogen shares were up 1-1/4 in late afternoon trading.
The drug is now before the European Commission for final review and approval, which, if granted, would allow Biogen to market the drug in all 15 member states of the European Union.
"The likelihood of it not getting approved now is extremely low," said David Molowa, an analyst with Bear, Stearns & Co Inc. "I would expect formal approval in March or April," he said.
Approximately 300,000 to 350,000 Europeans suffer from the disease, which leads to degeneration of the sheath of myelin protecting the nerves in the brain and spinal cord.

MS is more common among women and it usually first strikes between the ages of 20 and 40. About 60 percent of MS patients suffer from flareups of the disease interrupted by months or years of remission, Biogen said.
If approved for sale, Avonex would compete head-to-head in Europe with Betaferon, manufactured by Germany's Schering AG, but it has already proven to be a formidable competitor in the United States.

In the United States, Schering's drug, licensed for sale by Chiron Corp of Emeryville, Calif., under the name Betaseron, has been on the market for more than three years compared with just six months for Avonex. But already Avonex has equalled Betaseron's market share in the United States, Molowa said. "I would expect (Biogen) to become the market leader in approved countries fairly rapidly," he said. "I believe it represents a major opportunity for the company."
In the United States, labels on Betaseron and Avonex both claim the drugs reduce flareups of MS, but only the Avonex labels also claim the drug slows the disease's progression.
Molowa also said the side effects of Avonex have proven to be milder and the required doses are lower.

Biogen said it sold more than $27 million worth of the drug in the United States during its third quarter ended September 30. Approximately 250,000 to 300,000 people suffer from MS in the United States.

Israel's Teva Pharmaceutical Industries Ltd TEVI001. took a step toward launching its own MS drug, Copaxone, in the United States in September when it won approval from a U.S. Food and Drug advisory panel.
Molowa estimates the European market at about $250 million on an annualized basis and Betaferon currently has about a $50 million share.

Biogen has arranged for Swedish pharmaceutical giant AB Astra ASTRAb.ST to distribute and market Avonex in the Nordic countries and Schering-Plough Corp has rights to distribute the drug in Spain. Other companies will distribute Avonex in Italy and Australia and New Zealand.
Biogen will sell the drug itself in some European markets, including France, Germany, the United Kingdom and the Benelux countries.
